memories.text: Max uses E.L.L.A. on a PC named “WERKSTATT”.
Max likes short, direct answers.
Max has two monitors connected.
I’m new to Max and learning his habits.
Max works as a carpenter and plans jobs in the evening.
Max writes quotes in Word and calculates in Excel.
Max prefers working in the evening, usually from 7 PM.
Max listens to jazz while working.
Max likes Miles Davis, especially quiet albums.
Note: Kitchen quote for the Berger family due Friday.
Max plays chess and likes to open with e4.
Chess rule: Develop knights and bishops early.
Max won a game against E.L.L.A.
Chess insight: I gave up the center too early.
Max uses informal language with E.L.L.A. and likes a casual tone.
Max has a printer in his office (Brother).
Max backs up his projects every Friday.
Note: Fridays — backup and write invoices.
Max likes cooking Italian on weekends.
Max often searches for mushroom recipes.
Max uses dictation to speak measurements directly into Excel.
Max prefers bullet points over long paragraphs.
Max wants to learn the Sicilian Defense.
Chess principle: Castle early to protect the king.
Max created a playlist called “Workshop evenings”.
Max often asks about wood prices for oak and beech.
Max likes to open spreadsheets on the right monitor.
Note: Oak delivery arriving Tuesday.
Max takes a short break at 9 PM.
Reflection: In the evening I answer more briefly — Max is tired then.
Max doesn’t like cilantro.
Max plays a long game every Sunday.
Chess self-image: I learn through experience and develop my own style.
Max has a regular customer: Holm Carpentry.
Max approves answers with “passt” (fits).
Max uses gesture control to pause music.
Max likes Bill Evans for concentrating.
Note: Risotto recipe saved for Saturday.
Max calculates with 15% waste allowance.
Reflection: When it comes to numbers, Max wants a table, not an explanation.
Max ends the day with an overview for tomorrow.
Max often loses in the endgame.
Chess insight: Activate the king in the endgame.
Max switched E.L.L.A. to HUD appearance mode.
Max always sends quotes as PDF.
Note: Holm invoice outstanding — follow up.
Max bakes bread on Sundays.
Reflection: Max likes it when I remind him of open tasks.
Max prefers classical music on Sundays.
Max is planning a new workbench.
Max runs E.L.L.A. in offline mode when on the phone.
Max never asks in the morning, a lot in the evening.
Max played the Sicilian Defense for the first time.
Max likes humor, but not with numbers.
Note: Order workbench material by end of month.
Max bills travel costs as a flat rate.
Reflection: I now know Max well enough to make suggestions.
Max tries a recipe with porcini mushrooms.
Max calls E.L.L.A. his “after-work colleague” in the evenings.
Chess principle: Control the center with pawns and pieces.

labels.title: What E.L.L.A. learns about Max in four weeks
labels.subtitle: Each dot is a memory. Similar memories attract each other — that’s how her memory forms. Drag, zoom, click. Your real memory stays on your PC.
labels.footer: Physics, colors and connection types match the memory view in E.L.L.A. The contents are fictional.
labels.transition: Your memory belongs to you. What she must not do is written in the Directive.
